positions.summary_short: Edgell would commit dedicated funding to Markham's active transportation plan, connect the fragmented bike network, and push protected cycling infrastructure on major roads.
summary_bullets: Supports dedicated and predictable funding for cycling and active transportation in Markham's capital budgets.

The Active Transportation Master Plan recommended $5.4M per year in capital funding; the 2025 budget gave $4.3M and 2026 $2.2M – 'The Mayor's budgets have not provided enough funding to meet the Plan's goals' (the City spent $33.6M on road widening in 2024).
Three term commitments: connect the disconnected bike network; increase Vision Zero targets and interventions; work with York Region so regional AT facilities integrate with Markham's network.
Yes to protected cycling infrastructure on appropriate arterial and collector roads, even where it reallocates road space; would strongly advocate to the Province and Region on regional roads.
Notes the Ontario government is 'notably hostile to active transportation facilities' and commits to strong advocacy for AT in all forms.
positions.verbatim_quote: As Mayor, I would make funding predictable and committed.
positions.source_title: Stephen Edgell - Mayor Candidate (Markham Cycles questionnaire responses)

positions.summary_short: Edgell would lower school-zone speed limits to 30 km/h, bring back speed cameras where allowed, and prioritize active transportation within neighbourhoods.
summary_bullets: Would lower the speed limit to 30 km/h in school zones (as Toronto did in 660 locations); re-implement speed cameras in school zones if the Province allowed.
Would prioritize active transportation within neighbourhoods first and ensure connections between neighbourhoods exist.
positions.verbatim_quote: Infrastructure is not permanent; we built it, and we can change it if it no longer suits our needs. I would prioritize active transportation within neighbourhoods first, and ensure connections between neighbourhoods exist.
positions.source_title: Stephen Edgell - Mayor Candidate (Markham Cycles questionnaire responses)

positions.summary_short: Edgell accepts that properly maintaining infrastructure may require higher taxes, saying residents appreciate the value for money.
summary_bullets: On cycling-route maintenance: 'Maintenance is, put simply, just a matter of sufficient staff resources and funding.'
Accepts that adequate maintenance 'may result in increased taxes, but I believe that residents appreciate the value for money of maintenance.'
positions.verbatim_quote: The uncomfortable truth is that this may result in increased taxes, but I believe that residents appreciate the value for money of maintenance.
positions.source_title: Stephen Edgell - Mayor Candidate (Markham Cycles questionnaire responses)

positions.summary_short: Ross campaigns on three pillars — resident safety, taxes and City Hall accountability — casting himself as a defender of taxpayers.
summary_bullets: Campaigning on three pillars: resident safety, taxes, and City Hall accountability.
Casts himself as a defender of taxpayers against a City Hall he says prioritizes winning over helping families.
positions.verbatim_quote: Martin Ross is a candidate for mayor of Markham, Ontario, in the 2026 municipal election, campaigning on three pillars: resident safety, taxes, and City Hall accountability.
positions.source_title: Martin Ross sponsored campaign message in the Hello Markham election issue

positions.summary_short: Ross pairs protection with compassion on safety, citing an incident where he persuaded a robber to return stolen goods and then bought the man dog food.
summary_bullets: On safety, pairs protection with compassion.
Cites persuading a robber to return stolen goods at a Markham Shoppers Drug Mart, then buying the man dog food.
positions.verbatim_quote: On safety, he pairs protection with compassion, a quality on display when he persuaded a robber to return stolen goods at a Markham Shoppers Drug Mart — then bought the man dog food.
positions.source_title: Martin Ross sponsored campaign message in the Hello Markham election issue

positions.summary_short: Ross promises a City Hall that serves residents instead of fighting them, with safeguards so municipal power is never turned against residents.
summary_bullets: Core promise: a City Hall that serves residents instead of fighting them – 'with safeguards so municipal power is never turned against residents'.
Campaign slogan: 'New Voice. New Markham. Vote Martin Ross for Mayor'.
positions.verbatim_quote: His core promise is a City Hall that serves residents instead of fighting them — with safeguards so municipal power is never turned against residents.
positions.source_title: Martin Ross sponsored campaign message in the Hello Markham election issue

positions.summary_short: Scarpitti tabled a $309.3M operating and $160.4M capital 2026 budget – his first Strong Mayor Budget – with $53.8M for roads and $34.5M for flood control.
summary_bullets: Budget 2026 ('Markham Racing Forward'): $160.4M capital budget alongside a $309.3M primary operating budget.
Capital spending: $53.8M on new road construction, repairs, rehabilitation and traffic improvements; $34.5M on flood control and stormwater; $12.1M on parks and trails; $15.8M on facility repairs.
First Strong Mayor Budget, introduced in the 2025-26 fiscal cycle.
positions.verbatim_quote: Markham's Budget 2026 demonstrates the City's continued track record of prudent fiscal management while making important investments in infrastructure and community initiatives.
positions.source_title: Mayor Frank Scarpitti tables Budget 2026: Markham Racing Forward (city news release)

positions.summary_short: Scarpitti used his strong mayor powers to veto as-of-right fourplexes on single-dwelling lots, citing impacts on transportation and parking.
summary_bullets: Used strong mayor powers to veto a council decision to allow multi-residential development (up to four units) on single-dwelling residentially zoned land.
Said permitting four units could 'potentially interfere with provincial and City priorities, including but not limited to adversely impacting transportation networks, parking capacity'.
Federal government had asked Markham to adopt the rule to access Housing Accelerator Fund money.
positions.verbatim_quote: It is my opinion that permitting up to four units on certain City properties could potentially interfere with provincial and City priorities, including but not limited to adversely impacting transportation networks, parking capacity.
positions.source_title: Global News reporting on Scarpitti's use of strong mayor powers to block four units as-of-right

positions.summary_short: Scarpitti backs the Markham Stouffville Hospital expansion and a residential hospice, and wants more support for seniors aging at home.
summary_bullets: Honorary Patron of the Markham Stouffville Hospital Capital Campaign; supports the hospital expansion.
Committed to supporting the building of a residential hospice.
Seniors should be able to stay in their homes as long as possible; municipalities and senior governments need to do more.
positions.verbatim_quote: As Honourary Patron of the Markham Stouffville Hospital Capital Campaign, I will continue to lend my support and leadership, and commit to doing the same for a residential hospice.
positions.source_title: Mayor Frank Scarpitti's Inaugural Address (city news release)

positions.summary_short: Scarpitti says the province's 44,000-unit housing target more than doubles Markham's pace, demands matching senior-government funding, and insists growth pays for growth.
summary_bullets: Built 6,000 new housing units in the last term (~1,500/year); province targets 44,000 new residential units in Markham over 10 years – 'more than doubles the pace of our construction'.
Growth must be paired with doubled funding from senior governments for rapid transit, schools and hospitals.
'Growth needs to pay for growth' and a practical financial framework to deliver complete communities.
Locally: expand the network of community amenities, parks, trails and active transportation.
positions.verbatim_quote: Growth needs to pay for growth and one thing is for sure, we need a practical financial framework to deliver complete communities.
positions.source_title: Mayor Frank Scarpitti's Inaugural Address (city news release)

positions.summary_short: Collucci is running for Regional Councillor on an 'Our Home. Our Future.' theme, promising Markham a strong voice at York Region.
summary_bullets: Campaign theme: 'Our Home. Our Future.'
Approach: 'proven in public service, experienced in business and focused on the future'.
Aims to bring that combination of experience and forward thinking to York Region and 'ensure Markham continues to have a strong voice at the table'.
Endorsed by departing Deputy Mayor Michael Chan.
positions.verbatim_quote: My approach is simple: proven in public service, experienced in business and focused on the future. I want to bring that combination of experience and forward thinking to York Region and ensure Markham continues to have a strong voice at the table.
positions.source_title: Amanda Collucci campaign launch: three-term Markham councillor launches city-wide campaign with Michael Chan's endorsement (campaign press release)
